articles.title: The Dukes of Northumberland owned the 9,400-acre Rothbury Estate for about 800 years; now more than 25,000 people from 50 countries have helped raise about £30 million so it can be bought for wildlife
articles.summary: For nearly eight centuries, the Rothbury Estate in Northumberland remained in the hands of the Percy family, whose descendants include the Dukes of
articles.body: For nearly eight centuries, the Rothbury Estate in Northumberland remained in the hands of the Percy family, whose descendants include the Dukes of Northumberland. Now, after a two-year fundraising campaign that drew support from more than 25,000 people across over 50 countries, the 9,486-acre estate has been acquired by The Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust for nature conservation, as per a report by The Guardian. The charities announced the successful purchase on October 30, 2026, describing it as a rare opportunity to restore wildlife habitats across a vast stretch of northern England.The campaign, which sought to raise around £30 million, brought together individual donors, charitable foundations, philanthropists and government support. According to The Wildlife Trusts, members of the public contributed more than £17 million, while a £5 million grant from The National Lottery Heritage Fund and a £1.94 million grant pledged by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) helped push the appeal towards its target. Donations also came from more than 50 countries, including Finland, Barbados, Kenya and New Zealand.The charities said they had taken out a low-interest loan to bridge the short-term gap between the money already received and donations and pledges still due, allowing them to complete the purchase of the entire estate. The campaign was launched in 2024, after the land was put up for sale by Lord Max Percy, the youngest son of the Duke of Northumberland. The Guardian reported that the estate was the largest area of land in single ownership to come up for sale in England in more than 30 years.A landscape with a rich wildlife populationLocated in Northumberland, close to the Scottish-English border, the estate covers around 3,800 hectares and includes moorland, woodland, rivers, grasslands and farmland. Its landscape is dominated by the Simonside Hills, which overlook the Coquet Valley and offer views towards the North Sea. The estate also contains parts of the distinctive Whin Sill geological formation, created around 295 million years ago when molten rock rose from deep underground and cooled.The area is home to several species that conservationists hope to protect and help recover. Curlews, lapwings and other wading birds inhabit its uplands, while mountain bumblebees forage across its grasslands. Its woodlands provide shelter for endangered red squirrels, and the estate is also home to cuckoos and merlins, the UK's smallest falcon.The rivers and surrounding woodland support salmon, critically endangered eels and birds such as wood warblers, redstarts and pied flycatchers. In spring, skylarks can be heard above the grasslands, while wildflowers including harebells, wild thyme and mountain pansies add colour to the landscape during warmer months.The Wildlife Trusts believes the estate could support an even greater variety of wildlife if habitats are restored and connected. Its longer-term ambitions include encouraging the return of species such as pine martens and beavers, alongside improving conditions for animals already living there.Part of a much bigger conservation planThe acquisition is intended to form the centrepiece of a proposed 40-mile nature corridor stretching from Druridge Bay on the Northumberland coast towards the Kielderhead and Whitelee Moor National Nature Reserves near the Scottish border. The plan aims to connect habitats across the region, allowing wildlife to move more freely through the landscape rather than remain confined to isolated patches.The Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust have said they want to make nature recovery compatible with farming and the needs of local communities. Their plans include restoring habitats, supporting nature-friendly and regenerative farming, improving public access and creating opportunities for people to learn about the estate's natural and cultural history. The charities have also stressed that the purchase is not intended to simply turn the entire estate into an inaccessible wildlife reserve. Instead, they want to work with farmers, land managers and residents to develop a model in which conservation and productive rural businesses can coexist.The project has, however, attracted some criticism. As The Guardian reported, some farmers and local representatives have raised questions about the potential impact of changes to traditional land management, food production and the profitability of farms operating on the estate. The Wildlife Trusts has said it intends to work with those who live and work on the land.A campaign backed by David AttenboroughThe fundraising drive also received high-profile support from broadcaster and naturalist Sir David Attenborough, president emeritus of The Wildlife Trusts. His backing reportedly generated more than £1 million in donations in just one week, giving the campaign a significant boost. Attenborough welcomed the successful acquisition, saying the opportunity would allow nature, communities, farming and heritage to come together. He thanked the thousands of people who had contributed, describing the project as a chance to create something valuable for future generations.The charities had already begun research and conservation work on sections of the estate acquired in October 2024. Volunteers, local community groups, archaeologists, birdwatchers and academics have helped document its wildlife, landscape and history. New citizen-science projects are also planned, including reptile surveys, soil-health testing and acoustic monitoring to record the sounds of wildlife. The purchase marks the end of the fundraising campaign, but the conservation work is only beginning.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Three English-born painters helped invent the way Canada pictured itself: how the Group of Seven made a nation’s landscape their subject
articles.summary: Discover how the Group of Seven, featuring three British-born painters, redefined Canada’s identity by focusing on its breathtaking landscapes and straying from European artistic traditions. Explore their contributions and the implications of their depictions of nature on indigenous histories.
articles.body: A country's identity can take shape through the images people associate with it. The paintings of huge forest areas, rugged coastlines, lakes and mountains played an important role in forming the image of Canada. It was a number of artists who made Canada’s landscape the main subject of their paintings. Three of the group’s seven founders were born in England before moving to Canada. Arthur Lismer, J.E.H. MacDonald and Frederick Varley were among the seven painters who created the Group of Seven. They were the artists who sought to form a distinct image of Canadian art, which would be independent of European traditions of painting.Three English-born artists became founding members of the Group of SevenThe original Group of Seven comprised Franklin Carmichael, Lawren Harris, A.Y. Jackson, Franz Johnston, Arthur Lismer, J.E.H. MacDonald and Frederick Varley according to the Art Gallery of Ontario and Parks Canada. Of all these, three were Englishmen. Arthur Lismer was born in Sheffield, England, in 1885 and his childhood friend Frederick Varley was born in the same city in 1881, the Canadian Encyclopedia notes. J.E.H. MacDonald was born in Durham, England, in 1873 and moved to Canada with his family in 1887, at the age of 14, according to the Art Gallery of Ontario and Google Arts and Culture. The Canadian Encyclopedia says Arthur Lismer immigrated to Toronto in 1911, where he worked at Grip Engraving Company. Frederick Horsman Varley followed him to Toronto in 1912. Their ways somehow crossed with the artistic circles of Toronto. All these artists who later formed the Group of Seven had been employed at Grip Limited, a commercial design firm in Toronto, where their professional bond began and they shared a passion for the art of Canada. The Art Gallery of Ontario’s history of the Group of Seven documents the artists’ backgrounds and their contributions to the movement.Tom Thomson influenced the group’s approach to Canadian landscapesTom Thomson had close associations with the artists, even though he was never part of the Group of Seven. His paintings of Algonquin Park were instrumental in defining the style the group adopted when painting landscapes. He employed expressive colours and loose brushwork when painting the mood of the natural environment. His paintings inspired the artists to paint scenes other than traditional landscapes of Europe. His paintings depicted the Canadian wild through an expressive style of painting. He passed away in 1917, after drowning in Canoe Lake in Algonquin Park. The West Wind is one of his best-known paintings.The Group of Seven held its first exhibition in 1920The group first used the name Group of Seven at its first exhibition held on May 7, 1920, at the Art Gallery of Toronto, currently known as the Art Gallery of Ontario. Their paintings revolve around the forest, lakes, rocky landscapes and changing seasons of Canada. They chose not to adopt the conventional way of painting landscapes and chose simplified shapes, bold colours and expressive strokes instead. Their early artwork was based mostly on the landscape of northern Ontario, but gradually spread all over Canada. This is why Parks Canada honoured it as a national historical event in 1974.Lismer, MacDonald and Varley developed different artistic styles Despite the common interest in the natural surroundings in Canada, each of the three artists had a distinctive approach to the group. Thus, Arthur Lismer gained fame due to his landscapes of Georgian Bay as well as other Ontario landscapes. His works had characteristic features of rhythmic shapes and vivid colours. He also became a leading art educator, serving as principal of the Victoria School of Art and Design in Halifax from 1916 to 1919, The Canadian Encyclopedia notes. J.E.H. MacDonald devoted his landscape paintings to experiments with colour, composition and atmosphere. The landscape included those of Algoma and the Rocky Mountains. J.E.H. MacDonald also worked as a designer, poet and educator, thus encouraging people’s interest in Canadian landscape paintings.Frederick Varley gained recognition for both his landscape paintings and portraits. His paintings were notable for expressive use of colours and peculiar composition. Varley was an official artist of World War I.The group’s portrayal of Canada left out indigenous historiesThe work of the Group of Seven contributed to making forests, lakes and mountains recognisable icons of Canada. Nevertheless, the paintings of the group depicted these lands as pristine and devoid of human life, featuring only a few figures. Such depictions fail to portray the real history of the areas that were being painted, since most of the lands depicted in the works belonged to the territories of indigenous people and had their inhabitants. For example, Algonquin Park belongs to the traditional lands of the Algonquin Anishinaabe Nation. Thus, the work raised the issue of the way of depicting Canadian landscapes as well as the representation of the nation in general.The Group of Seven’s influence continued beyond its exhibitionThe original group dissolved itself in 1933. However, its legacy lived on through the Canadian painters and cultural institutions. The members of this group had formulated a style for landscape paintings that future painters would have to learn from, adopt or refute. Arthur Lismer, J.E.H. MacDonald and Frederick Varley introduced their knowledge gained in England to the emerging Canadian art movement. In collaboration with four other painters, they developed the language that helped Canada identify itself with its natural environment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Why Kim Jong Un's daughter could inherit North Korea
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's daughter, Kim Ju Ae, is increasingly being viewed as his potential successor, with several defectors believing that she
articles.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un's daughter, Kim Ju Ae, is increasingly being viewed as his potential successor, with several defectors believing that she is being prepared to inherit power in the reclusive country.Several North Korean individuals who defected to South Korea were interviewed by the Associated Press; according to them, North Koreans have no role in choosing their future leader, and believe that a third hereditary transfer of power would be publicly accepted by the population.The succession question has gained attention as Kim, 42, has made repeated public appearances with his daughter over the past four years. Although little is known about her, her prominent presence alongside her father at major state events has fuelled speculation that she could eventually lead the country.North Korea has been ruled by three generations of the Kim family since its establishment in 1948. The country's leadership passed from founder Kim Il Sung to his son Kim Jong Il in 1994, and then to Kim Jong Un in 2011. Neither transition was accompanied by any known public resistance.The next succession will determine who governs a nuclear-armed country of around 26 million people, where political freedoms are severely restricted and the state maintains extensive surveillance.Most defectors believe Kim's daughter is his heirKim Ju Ae is reportedly around 13 years old. Since late 2022, she has appeared alongside her father dozens of times at high-profile events, including weapons tests and military parades. North Korean state media has described her as Kim's “most beloved” and “respected” child.Her prominence has also been highlighted through official imagery, including photographs showing an elderly general kneeling before her and the teenager standing in front of her father.Former NBA star Dennis Rodman was the first to reveal her identity publicly, saying he had held Kim's daughter as a baby during a 2013 visit to Pyongyang.However, doubts remain over whether Kim Ju Ae will eventually take over, largely because she is a woman in a political system where women remain significantly underrepresented in senior positions.According to South Korea's unification ministry, only one of the ruling Workers' Party's 17 department directors is a woman. That position is held by Kim's younger sister, Kim Yo Jong, who is an influential figure in the country's leadership. South Korean officials also believe Kim Jong Un has another, younger child, although the sibling's gender has not been confirmed.Lee Si-young, a North Korean defector who heads Seoul-based Free North Korea Radio, said some of her older contacts in North Korea were unhappy with the prospect of a woman taking power. However, she said members of the Kim family were regarded as “gods reigning over humans”, adding that gender did not matter in determining the country's leadership.Why another hereditary succession may face little resistanceRegardless of whether Kim Ju Ae becomes the next leader, observers believe Kim Jong Un is likely to select one of his children to continue the family's rule. They expect such a move to encounter little resistance within North Korea, at least publicly.“North Koreans will passively accept a hereditary succession as something that they should go along with,” Ahn Chan-il, a defector and head of the World Institute for North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AP.The country's previous transitions offer some indication of how a future succession could unfold. Kim Jong Il had spent around two decades as his father's designated successor and worked alongside Kim Il Sung before taking over in 1994, when he was 52.The transition to Kim Jong Un in 2011 was less predictable. At 27, he was considered young and inexperienced by outside observers. He nevertheless consolidated his authority through a series of purges and high-profile executions, including the killing of his powerful uncle, Jang Song Thaek, in 2013.South Korea's intelligence agency has recently assessed that Kim Jong Un is extremely obese and faces a high risk of cardiovascular disease, although it has found no other indications of poor health. The assessment has added to attention surrounding the question of who could eventually succeed him.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A charity shop worker was accused by his mother of trying to murder his own brother; after she left him out of her £600,000 will, a court ruled in his favour
articles.summary: Peggy Dalton’s decision to leave almost all her £600,000 estate to one son and his wife was overturned by the High Court after her other son challenged
articles.body: Peggy Dalton’s decision to leave almost all her £600,000 estate to one son and his wife was overturned by the High Court after her other son challenged the will. Richard Dalton, a retired electrician who volunteers at a charity shop, had been excluded from his mother’s inheritance following allegations that he stole money from her and attempted to murder his brother. The judge found that dementia, isolation and possible undue influence had undermined Peggy’s ability to make a valid will, restoring an earlier arrangement that gave Richard a share of the estate.Richard Dalton wins £600,000 will dispute after murder accusationThe dispute centred on a dramatic change in Peggy Dalton’s wishes during the final months of her life. According to The Independent, her earlier 2018 will provided for her estate to be divided between Richard, his brother Robert and grandson Vincent. However, a new document signed in November 2020 removed Richard from the inheritance altogether, leaving almost everything to Robert and his wife Carly.The decision came after Robert and Carly moved into Peggy’s Surrey home in early 2020. The couple became closely involved in her financial affairs after a power of attorney was established, while concerns emerged about her growing separation from relatives and healthcare professionals.How did Peggy Dalton’s will change before her deathPeggy had experienced considerable family loss before the inheritance dispute began. Her husband William died in 2008 after suffering brain damage in a road accident, following years of care from Peggy. The family also lost daughter Christine in 2015 and son David in 2018, leaving Richard and Robert as her surviving sons.Under the 2018 will, Peggy’s estate was expected to be shared between Richard, Robert and Vincent. However, the November 2020 document represented a substantial departure from that arrangement. It provided £10,000 each for six grandchildren and divided the remaining estate between Robert and Carly.The Independent reported that Peggy told the will writers Richard had taken £100,000 from her and had been charged with attempted murder after attacking Robert. These allegations became central to the court proceedings, as Richard argued that his mother’s beliefs were mistaken and had been influenced by others.The family circumstances raised concernsRichard’s legal challenge focused on the circumstances in which the new will was made. His barrister argued that Robert and Carly had moved into Peggy’s home and increasingly controlled her daily life, finances and access to other people.The Independent reported that family members were unable to administer Peggy’s medication, while social workers were denied access. Medical professionals and relatives had also expressed concerns about Robert and Carly’s involvement in her financial affairs.There is a major difference between a genuine decision to exclude a relative and one made under pressure or based on incorrect information. Richard had never been charged with attempted murder, although he had been convicted of dangerous driving following an incident involving Robert and their mother’s car.According to the court evidence, Peggy had not witnessed that incident herself. The judge therefore questioned how she had come to believe Richard had attempted to kill his brother.Dementia affected Peggy Dalton’s ability to make a willMaster Katherine McQuail found that Peggy’s mental condition had deteriorated significantly by late 2020. The judge concluded that dementia had affected her ability to understand the document and the circumstances surrounding her decision.Peggy was hospitalised less than a month after signing the will and later entered a care home, where her dementia was described as quite advanced. Richard’s legal team argued that her condition made it unlikely she had been mentally capable of making such a substantial change only months earlier.The Institute of Professional Willwriters, explained that testamentary capacity requires a person to understand the nature and effect of making a will, the extent of their estate and the claims of those who might expect to benefit. Simply expressing a preference or holding a conversation does not necessarily establish that understanding.The institute also stressed that dementia and cognitive decline should prompt careful assessment rather than an assumption that a person can make legally valid decisions.Why did the High Court overturn the 2020 willThe judge declared Peggy’s November 2020 will invalid on several grounds, including lack of testamentary capacity, lack of knowledge and approval, improper execution and undue influence.Master McQuail found Peggy had been socially isolated from family members and medical professionals after Robert and Carly moved into her home. She decided that, even if Peggy retained some ability to make a will, her independent wishes had been overtaken by the influence of the couple.The judge also criticised the will-writing process. Robert and Carly were present when instructions were given, and the will writer had not spoken to Peggy privately or obtained medical evidence to establish whether she was mentally fit to make the document.The ruling restored Richard’s inheritanceThe High Court reinstated Peggy’s 2018 will, restoring Richard’s one-third share of the estate, estimated at approximately £200,000. Robert and Carly were also ordered to pay Richard’s legal costs, reported by The Independent at around £190,000.The ruling meant the couple’s inheritance could be substantially reduced by the costs order if they could not pay it from their own finances.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2016, a Michigan business redirected runoff into the home next door, flooding its basement and burning out five sump-pump motors; a November 2026 appeals ruling reduced the owner's damages from $170,000 to $102,000
articles.summary: The Michigan Court of Appeals has reduced damages awarded to a homeowner to $102,000 after a neighbouring business's drainage changes sent excess
articles.body: The Michigan Court of Appeals has reduced damages awarded to a homeowner to $102,000 after a neighbouring business's drainage changes sent excess rainwater onto her property, causing repeated basement flooding and damage to her house and garage. In a ruling issued Thursday, the court upheld the business's liability but revised the earlier $170,000 award after correcting the calculation of repair costs. The dispute involved homeowner Sherilyn Hart and North Waverly LLC, which owned the commercial property next to her home.According to the judgment, Hart and her husband, Anthony McCarty, bought the residential property in 2013. They planned to renovate it and rent it out, while living in their primary home next door. North Waverly LLC bought the commercial property immediately south of their house in 2015.The couple said they had not experienced excess water or flooding before May 2016. The problem began after the business changed its drainage system and connected its downspouts to two long, uncapped plastic pipes. One pipe discharged water directly onto Hart's property, while the other released water below ground near the boundary between the properties.McCarty raised the issue with North Waverly's managing member, Eric Stevenson. Stevenson told him the arrangement was temporary and that the pipe would be moved under the parking lot. McCarty warned him that heavy rain would cause water to collect on their property.The front pipe, however, remained in place for nearly six years, until 2021. The couple said their repeated attempts to contact Stevenson later went unanswered.Flooding damaged the house and garageThe excess runoff left the couple's yard saturated and caused water to collect around the garage and the eastern wall of the house. Water also entered the basement, damaging equipment and parts of the property.The eastern basement wall began bowing inward and eventually slid off its sill. The house had to be raised, and the wall was replaced in 2021. The north and south basement walls also needed repairs.The couple reported cracks in the plaster throughout the house, a roof leak that required drywall work and reroofing, and damage to the concrete driveway pad. They said the pad shifted and had to be reset using a skid steer.Basement flooding also ruined a new furnace, central air-conditioning unit and gas water heater. McCarty said five sump-pump motors burned out between 2016 and 2023. The homeowner's insurance did not cover the damage.McCarty estimated that repairs to the house would cost between $60,000 and $65,000. The estimate did not include most repairs to the garage. The records also contained bills for basement wall and sewer work, roofing, equipment rental, drywall and insulation, and a replacement water heater.Couple tried several ways to stop the waterThe couple contacted Stevenson and approached township and county officials about the problem. McCarty also contacted the Environmental Protection Agency in 2019.In 2018, he rented earth-moving equipment, dug a trench, installed a larger sump line and a commercial pump, and regraded the backyard. These measures were intended to manage the water collecting around the property.In June 2020, McCarty capped both collector pipes. He kept them covered for about 11 months, during which the soil gradually dried. After the caps were removed, he built a system in 2021 to carry the water back to the business's property. It used a sump crock and a PVC pipe that directed water over the retaining wall towards the commercial parking lot and storm drain.The system worked for about 90 days, and the soil dried within a week. However, the township issued a violation notice, and the couple removed it in early December 2021.The township had also issued a code violation to North Waverly in June or July 2021 over the condition of the retaining wall and the concentrated discharge of water. The business rebuilt the eastern retaining wall that year and buried the pipes in pea gravel near the property boundary.In 2023, it changed the pipe outlets again, placing them about four feet south of the boundary in a stone-filled drainage system. McCarty said this reduced the runoff and stopped further problems with the front pipe.Appeals court revises compensationHart and McCarty filed a lawsuit in 2022, accusing the business of trespassing and creating a nuisance through the excess water. The business denied liability and filed a counterclaim over part of the retaining wall that it said encroached on its property.After a four-day trial, the circuit court found that North Waverly's drainage changes had created unnatural and excessive runoff. It held the business responsible for trespass and nuisance and found that the water had caused substantial damage.The trial court initially awarded $150,000 for economic losses, $50,000 for emotional distress and mental anguish, and $40,000 in attorney fees. It later removed the attorney fees and reduced the economic damages by 20%, leaving a total award of $170,000.The appeals court upheld the findings of trespass and nuisance. However, it found that the trial court had miscalculated the repair costs. The court said the estimate of $60,000 to $65,000 covered repairs to the house, rather than the garage as the trial court had stated. It also found that some individual expenses appeared to have been counted more than once.The appeals court considered $65,000 a fair estimate of the economic damage. After applying the 20% reduction for the homeowner's share of responsibility, it set the amount at $52,000.The court also upheld the $50,000 award for emotional distress under the nuisance claim. It said the couple had faced nearly seven years of interference with their use and enjoyment of the property. Their exhaustion and loss of motivation to complete the renovation and rent out the house were among the reasons supporting the award.The court did not allow emotional distress damages under the separate trespass claim. It also rejected the business's adverse-possession counterclaim, finding that it had not established the required 15-year period of possession.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 13 California teenagers collect 22,000 discarded tennis and pickleballs in just 24 hours to set a Guinness World Record; all collected balls sent for specialist recycling, kick-starting an environmental movement
articles.summary: Thirteen teenagers in California have collected 22,000 discarded tennis balls and pickleballs in just 24 hours, setting a Guinness World Record while
articles.body: Thirteen teenagers in California have collected 22,000 discarded tennis balls and pickleballs in just 24 hours, setting a Guinness World Record while drawing attention to the growing problem of sports equipment waste. The record-breaking collection took place at Reed Park in Santa Monica on September 19, 2026, as part of a youth-led environmental initiative called Another Bounce. The students gathered approximately 1,213 kg (2,674 lb) of used sports balls, which were sent for specialist recycling rather than being disposed of in landfills. What began as a student-led effort to address waste at local sports facilities has developed into a wider campaign involving schools, sports clubs, community members and local authorities.Another Bounce: How a student project to collect discarded tennis and pickleballs became a world recordThe initiative, called Another Bounce, operates under the umbrella of Habits of Waste, a US-based environmental nonprofit. It was developed by student-athletes who noticed how frequently tennis balls and pickleballs were discarded after losing their bounce or becoming damaged.The students began collecting used sports balls in February 2026, placing dedicated collection bins at tennis clubs, schools and other sports facilities across the Los Angeles area. The campaign gradually attracted support from local players, families and sports organisations, allowing the teenagers to expand their collection network.The September 19 event at Reed Park brought the campaign to its record-breaking stage. Thirteen students representing five local high schools participated in the effort, with a Guinness World Records adjudicator present to verify the achievement. The final collection of 22,000 balls established a new record for the most sports balls collected for recycling in 24 hours.Why discarded tennis balls and pickleballs are an environmental concernTennis balls and pickleballs are frequently replaced because of wear and tear, creating a waste problem that receives relatively little attention compared with other forms of plastic pollution.Traditional tennis balls have a rubber core covered with synthetic felt, while pickleballs are generally manufactured from hard plastic. Tennis balls gradually lose their pressure and bounce, while pickleballs can crack or become damaged after repeated use. Once they are no longer suitable for playing, many end up being thrown away.According to estimates cited by Habits of Waste, more than 500 million tennis balls and pickleballs are produced and sold annually. The organisation also estimates that approximately 125 million tennis balls enter US landfills every year.The materials used in these products can persist in the environment for extended periods. Their disposal therefore presents a challenge for waste-management systems, particularly as participation in recreational sports such as tennis and pickleball continues to grow.How the collected sports balls will be recycledThe collected balls were sent through a specialist recycling process in partnership with Ridwell, a waste collection and recycling company. The process is designed to recover usable materials rather than sending the discarded equipment directly to landfills.Depending on the material and condition, the balls can be processed through different recycling pathways. Plastic components can be shredded, washed and converted into pellets that can serve as raw material for manufacturing. Recovered materials can also be used in products such as sports-court surfaces and other manufactured goods.The initiative aims to demonstrate that sports equipment does not necessarily have to become waste once it is no longer suitable for regular play. By creating collection points at sports facilities, the students are also attempting to make recycling more accessible to players and clubs.Teenagers push local authorities to address sports wasteBeyond the Guinness World Record, Another Bounce is campaigning for longer-term changes in how used sports equipment is collected and disposed of. The students have approached local authorities in Malibu, Santa Monica, Beverly Hills and Los Angeles, encouraging them to introduce measures that support sports-ball recycling.In August 2026, officials in Malibu expressed support for the students' proposal and invited them to submit a draft ordinance addressing sports-ball waste. The teenagers also want sports-equipment manufacturers to take greater responsibility for products once they reach the end of their useful lives.One of their proposals involves establishing take-back programmes through which customers could return used tennis balls and pickleballs to manufacturers for recycling. Such systems could help create a more organised collection network and reduce the volume of discarded sports equipment entering landfills.Habits of Waste and its wider environmental campaignsAnother Bounce is supported by Habits of Waste, founded by environmental campaigner Sheila Morovati. The nonprofit works to reduce unnecessary waste through public awareness campaigns, community initiatives and policy advocacy.Morovati has also founded Crayon Collection, a programme that redirects unused crayons from businesses and restaurants to schools and children. Habits of Waste has previously worked on campaigns addressing single-use plastics and unnecessary disposable items.Through Another Bounce, the organisation is extending its work to sports equipment, encouraging young people, recreational players, schools and manufacturers to reconsider how used products are handled. The students' campaign combines community participation with an effort to establish more permanent recycling practices for an often-overlooked category of waste.You use AI every day. articles.title: Over 2,000 teachers, students face political persecution in Bangladesh: Report
articles.summary: More than 2,000 students, teachers and academics across Bangladesh have faced alleged politically motivated persecution since August 2024, with cases
articles.body: More than 2,000 students, teachers and academics across Bangladesh have faced alleged politically motivated persecution since August 2024, with cases ranging from academic exclusion and physical attacks to criminal proceedings and forced resignations, according to a report released by human rights organisation JusticeMakers Bangladesh in France (JMBF).The report, titled Persecution of Teachers and Students in Bangladesh’s Higher Education Sector: Academic Exclusion, Coercion and the Struggle for Justice and Accountability (August 2024–October 2026), documented at least 2,051 victims across 229 higher education institutions between August 2024 and October 2026.The Paris-based organisation said its verified records included 1,569 students, accounting for 76.5% of the victims, and 482 teachers and academics, making up the remaining 23.5%.It alleged that they were targeted because of their political affiliations with the Bangladesh Awami League and its affiliated organisations, or their actual or perceived sexual orientation.The findings point to alleged violations including politically motivated disciplinary action, intimidation, physical assaults, restrictions on examinations, exclusion from campuses and residential facilities, and pressure on teachers to resign.Students face academic and residential exclusionAccording to the report, 575 students experienced informal academic exclusion, which restricted or prevented their participation in education. Another 219 faced exclusion from residential halls or hostels, potentially affecting their ability to continue their studies.A further 576 students were affected by incidents involving mobs or unidentified attackers, JMBF said.The organisation also cited broader monitoring figures indicating that more than 100 students and former students were arrested or taken into custody in connection with examinations. It said more than 10,000 students and former students affiliated with the Awami League were reportedly arrested or taken into police custody.JMBF estimated that more than 100,000 students and former students with actual, alleged or imputed links to the Bangladesh Chhatra League may have faced politically motivated persecution or serious interference with their education.The organisation clarified that these broader figures were estimates and not independently verified national totals of unique individuals. They may overlap with its verified records and should not be added to the 2,051 documented cases.Teachers face criminal cases, assaults and dismissalsThe report also documented several forms of alleged professional and physical persecution targeting teachers and academics.At least 132 teachers experienced academic boycotts or exclusion from professional activities, while 121 faced criminal cases or prosecution and 107 were subjected to inquiries or investigations. Another 86 teachers reportedly experienced physical assaults, and 24 were dismissed from their positions.JMBF said the findings raised concerns about academic freedom, institutional independence, equal protection under the law and the right to education.It also documented allegations of discrimination linked to actual or perceived sexual orientation, including humiliation, violations of privacy, coercive questioning and institutional punishment.The organisation stressed that political affiliation alone could not establish an individual's responsibility for misconduct. It said any disciplinary or criminal action must be backed by credible evidence and follow fair procedures, with those accused given an effective opportunity to respond.JMBF calls for independent investigations and international scrutinySpeaking at the release of the report, JMBF Founder President Advocate Shahanur Islam said universities should be centres of knowledge and critical thinking rather than spaces for political retaliation and discrimination.“Universities must be centres of knowledge, freedom and critical thinking—not places of political revenge, intimidation and discrimination,” he said.Islam said the organisation's documentation of 2,051 victims across 229 institutions pointed to concerns over academic freedom and fundamental rights.“No student should lose the right to education because of political identity, and no teacher should lose their livelihood for holding a different political opinion. Political affiliation is not a crime, academic freedom is not a privilege, and education must never become an instrument of collective punishment,” he added.JMBF called on the Bangladesh government, university administrations, law-enforcement agencies and other authorities to end politically motivated exclusion, intimidation and violence.Among its demands, the organisation urged authorities to ensure unrestricted access to campuses, examinations and residential facilities for eligible students, and establish independent mechanisms to review contested suspensions, expulsions, dismissals and other institutional sanctions.It also called for investigations into allegations of physical attacks, mob violence, coercion, unlawful detention and abuses involving law-enforcement personnel. The report urged authorities to protect academic freedom and prevent discrimination based on political affiliation, opinion or actual or perceived sexual orientation.The organisation further sought the restoration of educational and professional opportunities for those subjected to unjustified restrictions, along with appropriate remedies and compensation.JMBF called on the United Nations Human Rights Council, relevant UN special rapporteurs, UNESCO, the European Union and international human rights organisations to examine its findings and encourage protective measures.The report warned that the alleged persecution could have consequences beyond individual cases, affecting students' education, teachers' careers and the independence of higher education institutions in Bangladesh.You use AI every day. articles.title: Workers laying a sewer pipe under a building in Dendermonde, Belgium, found about 50 gold bars and piles of gold coins bricked into the cellar walls, worth an estimated 9 million euros, and no one yet knows who owns them
articles.summary: An ordinary construction job in Belgium turned into an extraordinary discovery when an 18-year-old student and his colleagues uncovered a hidden fortune
articles.body: An ordinary construction job in Belgium turned into an extraordinary discovery when an 18-year-old student and his colleagues uncovered a hidden fortune while working on a drainage project. The find, estimated to be worth €9 million (approximately ₹99 crore), has since prompted an investigation into the gold's origins and the question of who has the legal right to claim it. According to reports by The Guardian, BBC News and Belgian newspaper Het Laatste Nieuws, the discovery was made on August 11, 2026, at a former brewery property in Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde, around 30 kilometres north-west of Brussels. The workers were removing part of the building's foundation to make way for new sewage pipes when they came across the concealed treasure. The student, identified only as Kobe, was working a summer job with construction company De Brand. What initially appeared to be ordinary coins turned out to be part of a much larger collection of precious metal. As the workers continued excavating, they discovered gold bars and other pieces of bullion hidden inside the building's masonry.A treasure concealed for decadesThe gold was reportedly packed into a bag and sealed behind a bricked-up cellar wall beneath a villa known as the Brouwershuis. The property was originally built in the late 19th century for Theophilus Van Assche, a member of a wealthy local brewing family. According to The Brussels Times, the collection included gold bars and coins, while subsequent reporting by Brussels Signal put the number of numbered bullion bars at 49, alongside thousands of coins. The building's history has added another layer to the mystery. Brewing operations at the site began in 1899 and continued until 1970, after which the property changed hands.The former brewery is now owned by CAW Oost-Vlaanderen, a social welfare organisation that is renovating the listed property to accommodate offices and housing. The renovation involved stripping much of the building's interior, leaving its exterior walls standing. The gold came to light during this extensive work.Who could claim the €9 million fortune?Following the discovery, the workers informed the property owner and contacted the police. The entire collection was subsequently taken to a secure government facility in Brussels, where it is being held while authorities investigate its origins and establish its legal ownership. Investigators are examining whether the gold could have been stolen or connected to criminal activity. Only after its provenance has been established can the question of ownership be properly addressed, according to reports citing the East Flanders public prosecutor's office.There are several possible claimants. The descendants of the Van Assche family could come forward if they can establish a legitimate connection to the treasure. CAW Oost-Vlaanderen, as the current property owner, and the construction workers who discovered it may also have a claim under Belgian law. Local historian and former Dendermonde mayor Piet Buyse has suggested that the gold could have belonged to the Van Assche family, given their wealth and historical connection to the property. However, this remains a possibility rather than an established finding.The legal process could take years. According to Brussels Signal and German broadcaster ARD's Tagesschau, Belgian law allows a five-year period for potential owners to establish their claims. If no rightful owner is identified by 2031, the treasure could be divided between the finder and the owner of the property.A possible reward for the young workerFor Kobe and his colleagues, the discovery has already become an experience unlike any other summer job. The workers handed over the collection rather than attempting to keep it, recognising that its value and uncertain origins required police involvement. The discovery has also attracted attention from people claiming connections to the property's past. Tagesschau reported that police received messages from people in different parts of the world, including individuals suggesting that their relatives had once worked in the area. Some people have also come forward claiming links to the Van Assche family.For now, the gold remains secured in Brussels as authorities work to determine where it came from and who is entitled to it. If the legal process ultimately favours the finder and the property owner, the student who began the day digging trenches for a sewage pipe could find himself entitled to a share of a fortune worth millions.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Namo Yamuna River Safari' launched in Delhi in bid to boost tourism; 6-km cruise planned
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Tuesday launched the recreational ‘Namo Yamuna River Safari’ at Sonia Vihar, calling it a reflection of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Tuesday launched the recreational ‘Namo Yamuna River Safari’ at Sonia Vihar, calling it a reflection of people's deep-rooted faith and devotion to ‘Maa Yamuna’.The eco-friendly tourism initiative offers a 6-km round-trip cruise between Sonia Vihar and Jagatpur.Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal, Delhi cabinet minister Kapil Mishra and deputy chief minister Parvesh Verma were also present at the launch.Following the inauguration, Sonowal, Gupta and Mishra enjoyed a cruise ride on the Yamuna River.Addressing the gathering, Gupta said the initiative would offer Delhi residents a new recreational experience, which they earlier had to travel to other cities to enjoy."Today, we are all set to witness something truly special here in Delhi: the launch of the 'Namo Yamuna Safari' on the sacred Yamuna River. This initiative is about much more than just a cruise, a safari, or a boat ride; it is a reflection of our deep-rooted faith, love, and devotion toward 'Maa Yamuna'," Gupta told news agency ANI.Highlighting the facilities at the site, the chief minister said visitors would be able to enjoy a spectacular light-and-sound show, recreational activities and amenities for people of all age groups."This is a brand-new experience for the residents of Delhi, the kind of experience for which people previously had to travel to other cities and rivers. With a spectacular light and sound show, engaging recreational activities, and a wide range of amenities for both children and adults, this site has become a truly significant destination," Gupta said.Inviting people to experience the river safari, she said, "I invite the people of Delhi to come here and experience the 'Yamuna Safari' along the route from Sonia Vihar to Jagatpur. Bring your children to see the sacred Yamuna and enjoy nature."Highlighting the infrastructure development undertaken in the national capital, Gupta said projects worth Rs 1.25 lakh crore had been implemented under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in collaboration with Union minister Nitin Gadkari, to decongest Delhi."Under the leadership of PM Modi, and in collaboration with the esteemed Nitin Gadkari, projects worth Rs 1,25,000 crore have been implemented in Delhi to decongest the city. Large flyovers have been constructed, and new expressways have been built," she said.The chief minister also spoke about the government's environmental initiatives over the past 21 months, asking whether previous administrations had made similar efforts to balance environmental conservation with cultural celebrations."Looking at the work the government has done regarding the environment over the last 21 months, I want to ask the people of Delhi: did previous governments ever think or act in this manner, ensuring that we can celebrate our festivals while simultaneously improving the environment?" she said.Describing the government's approach towards development and preservation of traditions, Gupta said, "It is remarkable for Delhi to have a government that truly cares for the hearts of its people, looks after their happiness, upholds traditions, drives development, and preserves our heritage. This has never happened before."She also assured that Chhath celebrations would be organised on a larger scale this year, saying, "I assure you that this year, we will celebrate Chhath on an even grander scale than before."Meanwhile, Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal emphasised the importance of water and highlighted the Prime Minister's vision for developing the country's inland waterways."Water is the lifeblood of all living beings; no creature on this earth can survive without it," Sonowal said.Praising Prime Minister Modi's initiative in exploring the potential of inland waterways, he said the Prime Minister had undertaken studies and research in the sector after assuming office."Prime Minister Modi, a leader who has become an inspiration for the nation and is among the most popular leaders globally, took the initiative upon assuming office to study and research the country's inland waterways. The success of the event held today at Sonia Vihar-organised in collaboration with the Delhi Government, with the invaluable support of the local community-is a testament to the Prime Minister's formidable vision," he said.Delhi minister Kapil Mishra said the project was inspired by the Prime Minister's vision and described the river safari as a new tourism attraction in the national capital."It was PM Modi's vision and call to action that inspired the people of Delhi to entrust the BJP with the reins of governance," Mishra said.He said a recreational zone had also been developed at the site, featuring food, children's and entertainment zones for families."This magnificent project, the 'Namo Yamuna River Safari,' begins here at Sonia Vihar. In addition to this service, a recreational zone has been developed, a space where you can visit with your entire family. It features a food zone, a kids' zone, and an entertainment zone," he said.Mishra added that visitors would be able to enjoy a musical fountain show every evening, narrating stories associated with Lord Shri Krishna and the Yamuna River."Every evening, visitors, both residents of Delhi and those travelling to the city, will be able to enjoy a beautiful musical fountain show, which narrates the tales of Lord Shri Krishna and the story of the Yamuna River," he said.He further said more boats would be added in the future and water sports activities would also be introduced."More boats will be added in the future, along with water sports activities. As it stands today, this site has evolved into an international-standard tourism destination. It is within walking distance of the Sonia Vihar Metro Station," Mishra told news agency ANI.Delhi deputy chief minister Parvesh Verma said the launch reflected the coordination between the Delhi government and the Centre."Seeing the joy on people's faces today, it is evident that the Delhi government and the Government of India are working well together," he said.Expressing concern over the condition of the Yamuna, Verma said the river had gradually lost its identity over the past two decades."Over the last 20-25 years, the Yamuna, which we can still identify as a river on Google Maps, was gradually reduced to little more than a large, open drain. Our connection to it slowly faded away," he said.Verma urged residents to help keep the river clean by refraining from dumping plastic waste and religious offerings into it."While the government will do its part, every resident of Delhi must also play their role: we must not discard plastic or religious offerings into the river, and we must ensure the Yamuna is not polluted," he said.He added that the initiative should develop into a tourist destination while helping revive people's cultural connection with the river."Let this become a tourist destination for us-a place where a vital part of our culture is revived and brought back to life," Verma said.The ‘Namo Yamuna River Safari’ offers a 6-km round-trip cruise between Sonia Vihar and Jagatpur. The facility also has recreational zones, food outlets, entertainment options and a musical fountain show. More boats and water sports activities are planned for the future.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 1 killed as UP village head opens fire over gambling dispute; surrenders fearing encounter
articles.summary: VARANASI: One person was killed while another suffered a bullet injury after Bakrabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40, allegedly opened fire on them during a
articles.body: VARANASI: One person was killed while another suffered a bullet injury after Bakrabad village head Sanjay Bind, 40, allegedly opened fire on them during a dispute over gambling in Mohav village under Kotwali police station limits in Ghazipur district late Monday night.Police teams began raiding possible hideouts of Bind, but he managed to reach Kotwali police station on Tuesday afternoon and surrendered before the police.Ghazipur ASP (City) Rakesh Kumar Mishra said around 10 people were gambling near a pond at Pasipurwa in Mohav village on Monday night. Around 10.30 pm, Bind and his associates joined them. Witnesses told police that after an argument broke out, Bind pulled out a pistol and opened indiscriminate fire.The bullets hit Ajay Pasi, 28, of Mohav, and Surendra Ram, 35, of Islamabad village, while Bind managed to escape. Both injured men were rushed to Ghazipur Medical College. However, doctors found their condition critical and referred them to the trauma centre at BHU in Varanasi. Ajay died during treatment, while Surendra, a mason, remained under treatment.On receiving information, Ghazipur SP Vinay Kumar Singh, Mishra and other officials reached the spot and also met the injured men at the hospital. Later, several teams were deployed to arrest Bind.However, fearing a police encounter, Bind reached Kotwali police station carrying a placard stating that he was surrendering and turned himself in on Tuesday afternoon. He told the police that he had won Rs 1.5 lakh while gambling and that others tried to snatch the money, leading to the firing.Police said Bind has several previous cases registered against him, including one for attacking a police team during Holi celebrations. He has two other criminal cases against him. Following the Holi incident, he was arrested and sent to jail. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said only NCP leaders Sharad Pawar and Sunetra Pawar could clarify whether the two factions of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) would merge, asserting that neither had discussed any such proposal with the BJP.“If they (Sharad Pawar and Sunetra Pawar) decide to merge, they will come and tell us, because the merger cannot happen without us. Neither of them has told us anything yet,” Fadnavis told reporters on the sidelines of a Diwali gathering at his official residence, Varsha, in Mumbai.The remarks come amid renewed speculation over a possible reunion of the two NCP factions after several leaders of the Sunetra Pawar-led NCP, including Praful Patel and Parth Pawar, met NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar last week.Sharad Pawar was recently hospitalised with a chest infection.‘Unfair to compare Sunetra Pawar with Ajit Pawar’Asked to compare Sunetra Pawar's leadership with that of her late husband Ajit Pawar, Fadnavis said such a comparison would be unfair, noting that Ajit Pawar had decades of political experience and a deep understanding of Maharashtra.“Ajit Dada was a leader who had been tested over time. He had an immense understanding of Maharashtra and a deep knowledge of the state. Sunetra Pawar is now adapting to the situation. Comparing her with Ajit Dada would be unfair,” he said.The chief minister added that other senior NCP leaders were collectively managing the party.Ajit Pawar, who was the deputy chief minister and NCP president, died in an air crash on January 28. articles.title: 40 years, a world record, but an uncertain future: What's next for IAF's IL-76?
articles.summary: When the Indian Air Force (IAF) announced on November 7 that an IL-76MD had landed at Nyoma in eastern Ladakh at 13,629 feet, marking the highest-altitude
articles.body: When the Indian Air Force (IAF) announced on November 7 that an IL-76MD had landed at Nyoma in eastern Ladakh at 13,629 feet, marking the highest-altitude landing by the aircraft type anywhere in the world, the message was about capability. The airfield is around 25 km from the Line of Actual Control (LAC), and the landing demonstrated that India's largest Russian-origin military transport aircraft can still operate close to the frontier.The Gajraj: IAF's heavy-duty workhorseThe IL-76MD, known in the IAF as the Gajraj, was inducted on June 16, 1985, with No. 44 Squadron. India acquired 17 aircraft between 1985 and 1989.It was used in Operation Pawan in Sri Lanka and Operation Cactus in 1988, when it flew paratroopers to the Maldives. It also served during the Kargil conflict, evacuations from crisis zones, Covid-19 supply missions and disaster relief operations overseas.After the Galwan clash, the IAF airlifted more than 68,000 troops, around 90 tanks and nearly 330 infantry combat vehicles. However, the operation also involved C-17 and C-130J aircraft, so the IL-76 cannot take credit for the entire effort.The availability problemThe IL-76 can carry around 40 to 45 tonnes, but that capability depends on keeping the aircraft operational.In a 2017 report, the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) found that the fleet's average serviceability between 2010-11 and 2015-16 was just 37.99%, against the IAF's target of 70%.The lowest annual figure was 32.16% in 2010-11, which is the source of the often-quoted claim that barely one-third of the fleet was serviceable. However, this is a historical figure, not a measure of the fleet's current condition. An updated serviceability figure for 2026 could not be independently verified from publicly available information.Spares were the main problem. After the Soviet Union collapsed, the supply chain became fragmented. Fewer than 11% of spare-parts demands were met within 15 days, while more than 22% took over six months.A long-term maintenance agreement with Ilyushin, proposed in 2011, had still not been processed by April 2017. The fleet was subsequently reported to comprise 14 aircraft, primarily based with No. 44 Squadron.What nextIn 2024, the IAF issued a request for proposal to Russia's National Aviation Service Company to assess 11 IL-76MD aircraft and examine whether their operational lives could be extended from 2035 to 2050.The assessment also included the possibility of replacing their existing engines with PS-90A engines and upgrading their avionics. However, the proposal was for a feasibility assessment, not an approved modernisation programme.The IAF's plans to acquire medium transport aircraft in the 18-30 tonne category could replace some of the IL-76's transport roles, but these aircraft would not fully match its heavy-lift capability. The IAF also operates a fleet of just 11 C-17 Globemaster III aircraft.The challenge is no longer just to keep the IL-76 flying. It is to preserve the heavy-lift capability it provides until a suitable replacement is ready.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi was 'shocked' by Pranab Mukherjee's 'long-held desire' to be PM; his daughter asks why
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi has recounted how senior party colleague Pranab Mukherjee hinted at his \"long-held desire\" to become prime
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi has recounted how senior party colleague Pranab Mukherjee hinted at his "long-held desire" to become prime minister during a conversation in 2010, leaving her "shocked" with the suggestion that perhaps "it was time for a change at the top."The account in her newly released memoir, however, has drawn a sharp response from Pranab Mukherjee's daughter Sharmistha, who questioned why her father's ambition could have come as a surprise.Responding to Sonia's memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", Sharmishtha said there was nothing wrong with a politician aspiring to become prime minister, particularly someone with her father's experience in politics and governance."What's there to get 'shocked' about? Is it a crime to be ambitious, especially when that 'ambition' was supported by decades of experience in politics & governance, hard work & a brilliant mind?" she said.Recalling a conversation with her father, Sharmistha said she had once asked him whether he wanted to become prime minister. He had candidly replied that "any politician worth his salt has this ambition"."My father came from a very humble background. Whatever he achieved in his life was through sheer merit & hard-work. There was no-one to serve him positions, including PM-ship, on a platter due to dynastic entitlements. If a well-deserving person harbours ambition to become Prime Minister, what's wrong in that, unless Sonia ji was 'shocked' by the fact that anyone outside Gandhi-Nehru family could even dare to nurture such an ambition & furthermore dared to 'hint' it to her?" she said.Sharmistha also responded to Sonia's claim that Pranab Mukherjee never made her feel he held her response against him after she changed the subject during their conversation."In this same context, I read that she said she felt 'he never held it against me'. From what I read in his diaries & whatever conversation he had with me, I would like to reassure her that he DID NOT hold it against her or anyone else. He was a pragmatic person with deep understanding. He understood her reasons & insecurities that all human beings are prone to," she said.Also read: Sonia Gandhi memoir: BJP's Phoolka questions Army timeline, Indira's tears on 1984 riotsSonia on power-sharing with Manmohan SinghIn her memoir, Sonia writes that she was clear about Manmohan Singh being the prime minister and that, while she could offer him her opinions and suggestions as Congress president or disagree with him, it was her duty to defer to him."Further. I was determined not to be under any circumstance the cause of a misunderstanding that could give our opponents occasion to rejoice and weaken our government," she says in the book, which hit the stands on Tuesday.Former Congress chief describes an "unspoken division of responsibility" between the prime minister and herself, which she says worked smoothly: "the government under Dr. Manmohan Singh, and the party under me".She also recounts how the Congress leadership coordinated with the government through a core group that met weekly with the prime minister."A core group met weekly with the prime minister to ensure coordination between the two. Its other members were Pranab Mukherjee, who had been a minister in Indira Gandhi's cabinet in the 70s; the politically insightful Arjun Singh, a former chief minister of Madhya Pradesh; A K Anthony, a former chief minister of Kerala: and Ahmed Patel," she writes."We also met regularly as members of the Strategy Group, set up to discuss issues to be taken up in Parliament. Sometimes Pranab ji, as I always called him, would stay back for a chat," she says.What Sonia wrote about Pranab MukherjeeSonia recalls that Pranab Mukherjee had developed serious differences with then-finance minister P Chidambaram. During one such conversation in 2010, after expressing his frustration, Pranab made the suggestion that "surprised" her."He (Pranab) had developed serious differences with the finance minister P Chidambaram, and on one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become prime minister," Rajya Sabha member Sonia Gandhi says."I gently changed the subject, and though he may have been disappointed, he never made me feel he held it against me," she adds.Sonia points out that the Congress later nominated Pranab Mukherjee as the UPA's presidential candidate in 2012. He went on to win the election and become the President of India."I often called on him, mostly just to converse with the erudite and knowledgeable politician that he always remained."Sonia rejects 'back-seat driver' chargeAddressing allegations that she wielded the real power during the UPA years, when Manmohan Singh served as prime minister from 2004 to 2014, Sonia refers to what she describes as a "rash of stories" in the media. She says some of these accounts were fed by people close to the prime minister."A decade later, a book was published by one of his former aides, reaffirming the malicious and totally false allegations spread all along by my opponents: That I sent for files from the prime minister's office (PMO), interfered with administrative matters, and made key appointments," she says, rejecting the BJP's repeated charge.Sonia says the allegations that she interfered in the functioning of the government were particularly distressing, as she had always been careful to follow established rules."Though I had been the subject of worse accusations over the years, the fabrication that distressed me most was that I was looking into official files something improper for anyone outside the government. I had always been particular about adhering to rules, all the more so during this period," she says.She adds that the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) had issued a statement categorically denying that official files had ever been shown to her.Sonia also cites an interview in which Manmohan Singh's daughter Upinder Singh criticised a book by one of his former aides, describing it as a betrayal of trust and defending the relationship between her father and the Congress leader."Dr. Manmohan Singh's daughter Upinder Singh in an interview called the book 'nothing but a stab in the back. . . a huge betrayal of trust' and 'a mischievous, unethical exercise'. She affirmed that her father's relationship with me was one of 'mutual trust and respect'. However, the opposition and the media looked for every opportunity to spin the narrative that I was the government's 'back-seat driver'," Sonia says.She also gave details on why she turned down PM post after UPA victory in 2004.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: BJP's Phoolka questions Army timeline, Indira's tears on 1984 riots
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP leader and senior advocate HS Phoolka has challenged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's account of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence and Operation
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP leader and senior advocate HS Phoolka has challenged Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's account of the 1984 anti-Sikh violence and Operation Blue Star in her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, alleging that some of the details contradict official records and historical documents.He has questioned her account of when the Army was called in following Indira Gandhi's assassination and also disputed her description of the former prime minister's emotional reaction to Operation Blue Star.Speaking to news agency ANI, Phoolka said he had received several calls from media organisations seeking his response to Sonia Gandhi's account that the Army was called in on October 31, 1984, the day then prime minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated."I got several phone calls from media. They said Sonia Gandhi has written that during the 1984 Sikh massacre, the Army was called on 31st October itself. I have purchased the book to read whether this is indeed written in the book. If this is written in the book, it is against the records. It is absolutely false," Phoolka told ANI.Referring to the Misra Commission's findings, Phoolka maintained that the Army was formally called in only on the evening of November 1 and reached the affected areas in significant numbers on November 2.Phoolka also cited the commission's observations on the availability of Army personnel in Delhi during the violence."Misra Commission stated that 5,000 Army personnel were available within Delhi and they were not deployed. Misra Commission stated that had they been deployed, lives of 2,000 Sikhs could have been saved," he said.The Misra Commission found that an additional Army brigade of around 1,600 personnel had reached Delhi from Meerut before midnight on October 31, 1984.However, the Delhi administration delayed formally requisitioning Army assistance. The Army became operational in parts of central and south Delhi by the evening of November 1, while five additional brigades arrived on November 2. The commission observed that deploying around 5,000 available Army personnel on the morning of November 1 could have prevented at least 2,000 deaths."Phoolka also questioned Sonia Gandhi's account of Indira Gandhi's alleged remorse following Operation Blue Star, the military operation carried out at the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar in June 1984.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi reportedly recounts seeing Indira Gandhi watching a slow-motion recording of the operation's aftermath, with tears in her eyes. She describes the former prime minister's emotional reaction as an expression of pain and regret over the loss of lives during the operation.Disputing this account, Phoolka said it did not appear to be consistent with the historical record. He referred to a fact-finding report prepared by a team led by former Supreme Court judge Justice VM Tarkunde in September 1984, which he said included postmortem reports documenting the aftermath of the military operation."This doesn't seem to be true. In September, Justice Tarkunde's team wrote a fact-finding report on Operation Blue Star. Actual postmortem report was included in the report. The entire team was arrested and the report was banned," he told ANI.Questioning the account of Indira Gandhi's remorse, Phoolka further said, "If you look at the actual facts, you won't find any regrets or tears. It might be crocodile tears."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: After more than 20 years of Halloween builds, a Milwaukee couple transformed the fronts of three neighbouring homes into a Hogwarts-inspired attraction in 2026, while donations for homeless youth passed $100,000
articles.summary: In Milwaukee’s Bay View neighborhood, Halloween has become something much larger than a front-porch decoration contest.
articles.body: In Milwaukee’s Bay View neighborhood, Halloween has become something much larger than a front-porch decoration contest. A&J’s Halloween House, created by Andy Reid and Jamie Beauchamp, has spent more than two decades turning residential properties into elaborate seasonal worlds, and its 2026 Harry Potter-inspired display is the biggest version yet. According to TMJ4 and Hoodline, the attraction now stretches across three neighboring homes and has helped raise more than $100,000 for Pathfinders, a nonprofit supporting homeless and runaway youth.The display, located at 2943 S. Clement Ave., transforms the block into a miniature wizarding world. Visitors can find Hagrid’s hut, the Sorting Hat, Gringotts, the Great Hall, Dobby, a dragon, a giant spider, a troll and figures of Harry Potter and Lord Voldemort, all built into a sprawling neighborhood-scale set.A Hogwarts across three homesThis year’s display is not limited to one front yard. It spans three neighboring homes, giving the creators enough space to build a more immersive version of Hogwarts than they have attempted before. The result includes a Gringotts facade, Hagrid’s hut and a Hogwarts Express train car that visitors can climb into, as per the reports.Inside the train car, a video monitor makes it appear as though Milwaukee is rolling past outside the window, with dementors hovering in the sky. It is a small detail, but it captures the spirit of the display: the creators are not simply arranging decorations, they are building a world that rewards visitors who look closely.The attraction also includes moving portraits featuring Severus Snape, Albus Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall, along with an unexpected cameo by Dolly Parton. Jack-o’-lantern-themed Gringotts goblins add another layer of Halloween mischief to the wizarding theme, suggested the reports.Co-creator Andy Reid told TMJ4 that this year required “a crazy amount” of engineering, design and building. After more than 20 years of Halloween projects, he and Beauchamp have learned how to turn a neighborhood block into a destination.Two decades of buildingReid and Beauchamp have been creating Halloween displays together for more than two decades. Their work began with Reid’s memories of his mother’s elaborate Halloween decorations, and it has grown into an annual tradition that draws visitors from across Milwaukee and beyond.The Harry Potter theme is the largest display they have created so far, but it follows a long list of ambitious concepts. Previous years have included Scooby-Doo, Wheel of MisFortune, Ancient Aliens, Ghostbusters, Beetlejuice and a scary circus, according to TMJ4.The 2025 Scooby-Doo display was especially elaborate, featuring a two-story haunted mansion facade, a Mystery Machine replica and a pirate ship built with lumber donated by local supplier Bliffert Lumber. Earlier themes included a Wheel of Fortune scene in 2022 and an Ancient Aliens display with UFOs and pyramids in 2024.The creators store their materials in a garage between seasons, and some pieces are later donated to local schools. They do not disclose the cost of building each display, saying that the expense is their personal donation so that visitor contributions can go directly to the charity.A tradition of givingA&J’s Halloween House has partnered with Pathfinders for 11 official years. The nonprofit provides housing support, shelter for runaway and homeless youth, anti-sexual violence services and other assistance to young people in Milwaukee.Last year marked a milestone for the partnership. After a decade of fundraising, the display had raised $102,000 for Pathfinders, according to TMJ4. That total has since been surpassed, making the 2026 season another important chapter in the effort.The fundraising goal was set deliberately. Reid and Beauchamp had raised $84,000 by the end of the 2025 season and hoped to collect $16,000 more to reach $100,000. The milestone has now been passed, according to TMJ4’s reporting.Donations can be made at multiple collection points around the display. The setup makes it easy for visitors to contribute while enjoying the attraction, turning a neighborhood Halloween tradition into a practical source of support for young people in crisis.Why the cause mattersPathfinders was founded in 1970 by members of Plymouth Church, University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee faculty and local residents as a shelter for runaway youth. Today, the organization operates Milwaukee’s only dedicated youth street outreach team and serves about 5,000 young people each year, according to Pathfinders.The need is significant. A May 2025 report by the Wisconsin Policy Forum, cited by the Wisconsin Justice Initiative, found that Wisconsin K-12 student homelessness reached a record 20,195 students in the 2023-2024 school year. Milwaukee accounted for more than a quarter of the state’s homeless students and 40.7 percent of its unaccompanied homeless youth.Against that backdrop, A&J’s Halloween House does more than entertain. It gives neighbors a reason to gather, gives children a memorable experience and channels community generosity toward an organization that helps young people find safety and stability.A display with a deadlineThe Hogwarts-inspired attraction remains up through October, but it comes down immediately after Halloween. That short window adds urgency for visitors who want to see it before the creators begin dismantling another year of work.Reid has said that the team does not want people to expect an even bigger display next year, though he leaves open the possibility that they may make it better in other ways. After more than 20 years of building, the challenge is no longer simply scale. It is finding new ways to surprise a community that has come to expect something extraordinary.For now, the three-home Hogwarts display stands as both a neighborhood spectacle and a fundraising engine. It proves that Halloween can be more than costumes and candy, and that a front yard can become a place where creativity, community and compassion come together.You use AI every day.
